channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Feminist Media Batyr Jamal Launched in Kazakhstan to Combat Violence Against Women
item.description: Batyr Jamal, a feminist media outlet, was founded in Kazakhstan five years ago by Aysana Ashim. Launched on March 8, 2021, it focuses on women's rights, safety, and self-worth. The initiative arose during the 2020 pandemic amid reports of increased domestic violence. The media aims to address ongoing issues of femicide and violence against women, which remain prevalent despite societal changes over the past century.

item.title: South Korea Scrambles Fighter Jets as Russian Aircraft Enter Air Defense Zone
item.description: South Korean fighter jets were scrambled after Russian aircraft entered the country's air defense zone. The military issued an emergency alert as the planes approached Ulleungdo island before leaving the area. The incident prompted a swift response from the South Korean air force to monitor and intercept the foreign aircraft.

item.title: New Deputy Appointed to Uzbekistan's Ministry of Mining and Geology
item.description: Shamsiddin Alimov has been appointed as the new Deputy Minister of Mining and Geology in Uzbekistan. Born in Tashkent in 1984, Alimov holds degrees from Tashkent State Technical University. He previously held various positions at the State Committee for Geology and Mineral Resources and led the "Uzbek Geology Exploration" joint-stock company since 2023.

item.title: Four Cable Car Stations at Ala-Too Resort Connected to Electricity
item.description: Four cable car stations and several infrastructure facilities at the developing Ala-Too Resort in Kyrgyzstan's Issyk-Kul region have been connected to electricity. Nine out of ten planned transformer substations are installed, with the last one expected before November 25. The resort's first phase is scheduled to open on December 1.

item.title: Kazakhstan's First Anthropologist, Orazak Smagululy, Passes Away at 96
item.description: Orazak Smagululy, an academician of the National Academy of Sciences and a leading researcher at the Shokan Valikhanov Institute of History and Ethnology, has passed away at the age of 96. He was known for his research on the physical anthropology of Kazakhs and faced censorship for his work, including a book that was ordered to be burned by the Central Committee.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Faces Challenges in Utilizing Development Funds
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's regional development funds saw a significant increase in funding, reaching 5.2 billion soms by 2026. However, ineffective use and non-utilization of allocated funds have been identified in several districts. For instance, only 3.6 million soms of 19.3 million were utilized by the Issyk-Kul regional fund, and 105 million soms of 181 million remained unused in the Chatkal district.

item.title: Uzbekistan Publishes Draft Rules for Latin Alphabet Transition
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Justice has released a draft resolution for public discussion on the transition to the Latin alphabet. The changes will affect document processing, education, media, commerce, and state information systems. ID cards, passports, and driver's licenses will be issued in the new alphabet starting April 22, 2027, with existing documents remaining valid until January 1, 2028.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Surpasses Kazakhstan in Construction Growth Rate, Data Shows
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has significantly outpaced Kazakhstan in construction growth, with its building activity increasing 1.8 times in January-September 2026, compared to Kazakhstan's 11.5% rise. While Kazakhstan leads in monetary value of construction, Kyrgyzstan shows faster expansion in the pace of work.

item.title: Kazakhstan Fines Millions for Illegal Construction Near Water Bodies
item.description: Since early 2026, Kazakhstan has identified 18 cases of illegal construction on and near water bodies, resulting in fines totaling 12.7 million tenge. Authorities have also forcibly demolished unauthorized structures. These actions are part of efforts to enforce water resource protection laws.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Use AI for Legal Review and Corruption Risk Detection
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to implement artificial intelligence to review draft laws, identify legislative contradictions, and detect potential corruption risks. This initiative is part of the legal policy concept for 2027-2030. A unified digital system will cover the entire legislative process, from drafting to evaluation.

item.title: 424 Municipal Enterprises in Kyrgyzstan Rely on Subsidies, Facing Challenges
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has 424 municipal enterprises, many of which are dependent on budget subsidies and face operational issues. Some enterprises, like the Batken water utility, are fully funded by local budgets, while others, such as Batken Autobase, receive significant subsidies despite having non-operational vehicles. Irregularities in payment collection have also been identified.

item.title: Taliban Send Technical Delegation to Bangladesh to Inspect Drug Quality
item.description: The Taliban's Ministry of Public Health announced the dispatch of a technical delegation to Bangladesh to assess the quality of locally produced medicines. The five-member team will inspect drug manufacturing facilities to ensure compliance with production standards and prevent the import of substandard drugs into Afghanistan. This follows a previous report of Afghan traders requesting reduced quality for cheaper prices.

item.title: Kazakhstan Experts Debate Lowering Mortgage Down Payments Amidst Price Concerns
item.description: Real estate experts in Kazakhstan are proposing to allow mortgages with reduced or no down payments, arguing that lack of savings doesn't preclude repayment ability. However, concerns exist that making credit more accessible could fuel a new surge in housing prices and increase borrower debt burdens. Some experts suggest individual assessment of borrowers' financial stability.

item.title: Goldman Sachs Warns of Potential Further Decline in US Stock Market
item.description: Goldman Sachs predicts a potential new wave of selling on the US stock market next week. The bank's models indicate algorithmic traders could sell tens of billions more in stocks. Investors' doubts about AI infrastructure investments and a disappointing IPO have contributed to market uncertainty.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev Arrives in Jordan for State Visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has arrived in Jordan for a state visit. He was met by King Abdullah II and Queen Rania at the airport. Fighter jets escorted his plane. The main events of the visit are scheduled for November 24.

item.title: Number of Microcredit Recipients in Kyrgyzstan Triples
item.description: In January-September 2026, microcredit organizations in Kyrgyzstan issued over 76 billion soms. The volume of lending grew by 20.7%, and the number of recipients tripled to over 2 million. This growth is linked to the spread of short-term online loans, with most funds used for consumer needs.

item.title: Kyrgyz Prosecutor General Reports Official Accountability for Citizen Complaints
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Prosecutor General reported that 254 officials faced disciplinary action for violating laws when handling citizen appeals. This followed inspections revealing 478 violations. The president has instructed a fundamental change in how state bodies handle citizen complaints, emphasizing timely local problem resolution.

item.title: Eastern Libya Government Files Complaint with UN Security Council Over Drone Attack
item.description: The Eastern Libyan government, led by Osama Hammad, has filed a complaint with the UN Security Council regarding a drone attack on Russian ships in Benghazi port on November 22nd. They demand an urgent and independent international investigation into the incident, suspecting Ukrainian involvement and potential support from Western Libya.

item.title: Three Oil Tankers Explode in Strait of Hormuz Despite US Military Escort
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced that three oil tankers struck sea mines and exploded while passing through the Strait of Hormuz, despite being under extensive US military escort. The IRGC warned that the Strait of Hormuz is not a place for unauthorized routes or ignoring maritime warnings.

item.title: Official Reception Held in Jordan in Honor of Uzbekistan President
item.description: An official reception ceremony was held in Jordan in honor of the President of Uzbekistan. King Abdullah II and Queen Rania of Jordan welcomed President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and his wife at the Al-Husayniya Palace. The leaders greeted members of the official delegations of both countries.

item.title: Karakol Opens Training Center for Energy Workers on Live Line Work
item.description: A specialized training center for energy workers performing live line work has opened in Karakol, Kyrgyzstan, with an investment exceeding 55 million soms. The center, equipped with modern facilities and tools, has already begun training specialists. The program includes theoretical and practical training on electrical safety and live line techniques.

item.title: Kyrgyz Security Service Identifies Official Misconduct and Security Breaches
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKNB) has identified significant issues within state and municipal bodies, including violations of secrecy regimes, unauthorized contacts with foreigners, and abuse of official position. GKNB Chairman Maksat Asanaliev highlighted these problems, emphasizing their negative impact on public trust and state reputation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Construction Firm Fined 2.2 Million Som for Violations
item.description: Jalal-Abad authorities have fined construction company 'Dastan Grand House' 2.2 million som for violations found at four building sites. Inspections revealed breaches of construction norms, safety regulations, and workplace organization. The company was issued orders to rectify the identified issues.

item.title: Tajikistan's Wage Arrears Reach Nearly $1.5 Million, Primarily in Transport Sector
item.description: Wage arrears in Tajikistan, including previous years' debts, amounted to approximately 13.4 million somoni (nearly $1.5 million) as of early October 2026, according to the Statistics Agency. The transport sector, manufacturing, and agriculture account for the largest portion of this debt. While overall arrears decreased slightly in September, some sectors like construction saw significant increases.

item.title: EU Proposes New Sanctions Against Russia, Including Sports and Visa Restrictions
item.description: The European Commission has proposed a new package of sanctions against Russia, including a ban on Russian athletes competing under their national flag in EU sports events. The proposals also include visa restrictions for former Russian military personnel and further limitations on 60 Russian banks and digital currency platforms. These measures aim to restrict Russia's financial resources for the war in Ukraine.

item.title: NATO to Deploy AWACS Aircraft to Poland Following Missile Incident
item.description: NATO countries have agreed to deploy an AWACS aircraft to Poland to enhance long-range radar surveillance. This decision follows the incident where Russian missiles violated Polish airspace on November 20th. NATO reiterated its commitment to solidarity and readiness to defend all allies against any threat. The AWACS aircraft are equipped for early warning and air traffic control, aiding in directing fighter jets.

item.title: Afghanistan: 257 Killed by Mines and Unexploded Ordnance This Year
item.description: Afghanistan's National Disaster Management Authority reports that 257 people have died and 87 have been injured by mines and unexploded ordnance since the beginning of the current solar year. Children constitute the majority of victims, with 189 fatalities. Over 900 square kilometers of land remain contaminated.

item.title: Taliban Deploy 'Green Units' to Protect Afghanistan's Remaining Forests
item.description: The Taliban have deployed special units known as 'Green Units' to safeguard Afghanistan's remaining forests, according to the Associated Press. Approximately one thousand personnel are involved in patrolling forest areas, particularly in Kunar province, to prevent illegal logging and timber smuggling. Decades of conflict and deforestation have severely damaged the forests.

item.title: Armenia's draft constitution to legally abandon claims to Nagorno-Karabakh
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan presented a draft constitution aiming to legally renounce claims to Nagorno-Karabakh. Pashinyan stated this move is crucial for restarting Armenian statehood, promising peace and independence. Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev insists on this legal renunciation for a peace treaty, as the current constitution references reunification with Nagorno-Karabakh.

item.title: Uzbek President Writes Letter to Grandson During Flight to Jordan
item.description: During a flight to Jordan, the President of Uzbekistan wrote a letter to his grandson, sharing his thoughts and wishes. He explained that his responsibilities extend beyond his family to the future of all Uzbek children. The president emphasized his life's purpose is to ease people's lives and help them overcome difficulties, regardless of his position.

item.title: Turkmenistan Hosts International Conference on Transport and Communications
item.description: Turkmenistan is hosting an international conference and exhibition titled "International Transport and Transit Corridors: Connectivity and Development - 2026" and the XIX "Turkmentel - 2026" exhibition. The event focuses on enhancing digital transformation, implementing advanced technologies, and strengthening international cooperation in the transport and communications sector.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Arrives in Jordan for State Visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, accompanied by his wife, has arrived in Jordan for a state visit. Upon arrival, the distinguished guests were greeted by an honor guard. Leaders of both countries welcomed members of their official delegations and reviewed the honor guard.

item.title: Kazakh Family Injured in Oman Accident: Evacuation Efforts Underway
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is arranging the evacuation of four citizens injured in a traffic accident in Salalah, Oman. The family, including a minor, sustained injuries and underwent surgery. Air Astana has rebooked their return flights for November 27.

item.title: Iran's Stance on Nuclear Treaty Unchanged Amid Internal Debate
item.description: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister stated that while there is internal debate about withdrawing from the nuclear non-proliferation treaty, Iran's official position remains unchanged. He noted that membership did not prevent attacks on nuclear facilities.

item.title: Turkmenistan Foreign Minister Meets with US Deputy Secretary of State in Ashgabat
item.description: Turkmenistan's Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov met with US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau in Ashgabat on November 23. They discussed bilateral cooperation, focusing on expanding trade and economic ties, energy, and transport sectors, including trans-Caspian routes. Both sides affirmed interest in continued dialogue.

item.title: NATO Chief Urges Allies to Prepare for War, Citing Russian Threat
item.description: NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg stated that the threat from Russia affects all member states and urged allies to prepare for potential conflict. He emphasized that there is no longer a 'safe rear' in Europe, as Russian missiles could reach Lisbon or Rome in minutes, making all nations part of the 'eastern flank'.

item.title: Uzbekistan's initiatives on robot classification supported at World Customs Organization session
item.description: Uzbekistan's proposals on classifying anthropomorphic and zoomorphic robots were discussed at the 68th session of the World Customs Organization's Harmonized System Subcommittee in Brussels. The Customs Committee of Uzbekistan presented the issue, and its initiative to improve robot classification was supported by several states. Further consideration and a revised working document are planned.

item.title: Karakalpakstan education ministry addresses school heating system malfunction
item.description: The Ministry of Education and Science of Karakalpakstan responded to reports of a heating system failure at School No. 4 in Nukus district. The first building uses gas and coal, while the second uses electric heat pumps. A faulty gas meter in the first building caused the issue; a new meter is being acquired, and temporary coal heating is in place.

item.title: Israeli airstrikes in Gaza kill three, including UNRWA staff member
item.description: At least three people, including a UNRWA employee, were killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza on Monday, November 23. Adel al-Helou, the UNRWA staff member, died in an attack near Jabalia refugee camp. Another strike targeted a vehicle in western Gaza City, killing two more people. A US-backed ceasefire has failed to halt attacks.

item.title: Uzbekistan Drafts New Administrative Procedure Code to Streamline Justice
item.description: Uzbekistan is discussing a draft Administrative Procedure Code to consolidate existing legal norms and introduce new mechanisms for judicial process efficiency. The code aims to develop the institution of claims, strengthen legal guarantees for administrative acts, clarify court procedures, and enhance enforcement control.
